resources.string: Passwords keeps sign-ins and their two-step codes in a KeePass file, the kind KeePassXC opens on a computer.
That file is the only copy. Keep it in a folder that Nextcloud, Syncthing or a share copies somewhere else, or save a copy now and then: the copy is the backup. Nothing is sent anywhere by this app.
That password does not open this vault.
This file did not open as a KeePass vault: %1$s
The file could not be read: %1$s. If it was moved or its app removed, choose it again.
Opened from another app, for now. Choose it with Open a different vault to have it remembered.
Needs a key file too? Choose it
That key file could not be read.
The last save to this file may not have finished: the phone stopped part way. The copy from before that save is kept.
Put back the copy from before
Leave the file as it is
Choose the master password. It is the only way in: nobody, this app included, can open the vault without it.
The vault could not be written: %1$s
No two-step codes yet. Press + to add one, or bring in the codes from another authenticator in Settings.
Nothing in this vault yet. Press + to add a sign-in.
Press a code to copy it. They change in %1$s s.
Not saved to the file yet. Press to try again.
Changes are not saved: this file is read only. Press to save the vault to a file of your choosing; it becomes the vault from then on.
Read only: this file came from somewhere this app cannot write to. Press to save to another file if you want to make changes.
Saved to the new file. That file is the vault now.
Delete — it goes to the recycle bin; tap again
%1$s copied. The clipboard is emptied in %2$s seconds.
Changes not saved. Press again to leave without them.
Not saved: this file is read only. The change is kept while the vault is open; press the line at the top of the list to save it to a file you choose.
Not saved: %1$s. The file is as it was, and the change is kept while the vault stays open.
Not saved: %1$s. The file may be damaged; the copy from before is kept, and Settings can put it back.
The newer file could not be opened with this vault\'s password.
The vault file changed since it was opened: another phone or computer saved it. This change is not in the file yet.
Open the newer file (this change is dropped)
Save this version as a copy
Replace the newer file with this one
Replace — their change is lost; tap again
Hold the phone over the code. It is read as soon as it is in view.
Read a QR code in a picture
A screenshot, or a photo already on the phone.
A kAuth backup or its exported list, an Aegis export without a password, or a text file of otpauth:// links.
Or paste a link: otpauth:// or a Google Authenticator transfer link
No QR code found in that picture. A closer, straighter picture usually reads.
%1$s codes were found; the first one is used.
Hold the code in the square. It is read by itself; there is nothing to press.
That code isn\'t a two-step code.
Scanning needs the camera. Choose a picture instead, or allow the camera for Passwords in the phone\'s Settings, under Apps.
The camera could not be opened. Choose a picture of the code instead.
That is not a secret key: they are letters A to Z and digits 2 to 7.
Most sites use 6 digits, 30 seconds and SHA1. Change these only if the site says to.

These came through a Google Authenticator transfer, which has no place for how often a code changes: every one arrives as 30 seconds. If a site used 60, its codes will be wrong here; check each against the site once, and change it under Edit if need be.
Google Authenticator transfers count every code in 30-second steps. Check this one against the site once.
Nothing there that this app can read as a code.
That Aegis export has a password. Export again from Aegis without one, bring it in, then delete the export.
This is a kAuth backup. kAuth\'s master password opens it; it is used once, here, and not kept.
That password does not open this backup.
The file is the only copy of the vault, and a copy of it is the backup. It stays locked with the same master password.
Put back the file from before the last save
Each save keeps the file as it was, inside this app, until the next.
Put back — this replaces the vault file; tap again
The file from before the last save is back. Unlock to see it.
The copy from before could not be put back.
This vault also needs a key file. Change its password in KeePassXC on a computer.
The vault is written again at once, locked with the new password. A copy saved before still opens with the old one.
Lock when away from the app
It also locks whenever the screen goes dark.
A short tick each time the codes change, while they are on screen. It follows the phone\'s touch vibration setting.
Off. Press to choose Passwords as the phone\'s autofill service.
Remember the app a sign-in was picked for
Writes the app\'s name into the entry, so it is offered there first next time.
DuraSpeed may have stopped Passwords in the background. Press, choose Open, and switch Passwords on in its list.
From kAuth, Aegis, Google Authenticator, or otpauth:// links.
The file stays where it is; this app just stops opening it.
The copy could not be saved.
weak, guessable by a determined attacker with the file
fair for a website, short for a master password
Leave out look-alikes (l I 1 O 0 o)
Words from the EFF\'s large word list, 7,776 of them. Easier to type and remember than characters; six words make a good master password.
There is no app on this phone for that.
Nothing leaves the phone: the app has no internet permission. The vault is a KeePass file wherever you keep it, and that file is the only copy, so a copy of it is the backup.

KeePass files read and written by kotpass (MIT); Argon2 by Argon2Kt (MIT) and the reference Argon2 (CC0); the QR scanner from Calm QR by Jacob Moss (Apache 2.0), reading with ZXing (Apache 2.0); passphrase words from the EFF large word list (CC BY 3.0); codes and imports from kAuth by OK1CDJ (GPL v3); icons from Material Symbols (Apache 2.0).
There is no browser on this phone to open that with.
